    Expert answer compared with the agent

    09 · Product decisions

    Why the system is designed this way

    Customer problemChoice madeWhyWhat we acceptHow we validate it
    Too many alerts reduce trustNotify when a change affects the journey or needs attention.A platform change matters; a harmless timetable refresh does not.A traveller may prefer more updates.Alert open rate, opt-outs, false-alert interviews and later support contacts.
    AI can misread time or moneyUse fixed calculations for missed/not-missed and output checks for seat, ticket and money claims.These decisions must be repeatable and traceable.Missing inputs produce “cannot confirm” instead of an answer.Historical replay plus expert-labelled failure cases.
    Unlimited searching is slow and costlyUse one live-data check and one policy check for the first response.Most cases need a quick verified next step.Unusual cases take a second pass or go to support.First-answer latency, API calls per case, cost per resolution and human-route quality.
    Berlin → SalzburgThe timetable proves the 13:18 connection is missed because arrival is 13:52. AI is used to gather context and compare viable options; it does not perform the time arithmetic.
    10 · How the prototype is validated

    Evidence increases before customers rely on it

    1Historical replayRun completed Berlin–Salzburg-like journeys. Compare the workflow with known arrival, connection and support outcomes.Proves calculations and finds missing cases.
    →
    2Shadow modeRun on current journeys, but show nothing to customers. Compare its decision with actual outcomes.Proves live-data matching and drift.
    →
    3Support-assistA support agent sees the evidence and proposed response, then approves, edits or rejects it.Proves usefulness and exposes unsafe wording.
    →
    4Customer monitorA small opted-in group receives verified alerts and choices; carrier actions still require confirmation.Proves comprehension, trust and resolution.
    Gate before moving forwardEvidence required
    Decision qualityAccuracy and safe-abstention bar met by cohort.
    Customer protectionNo unsupported seat, ticket, money or carrier-action claim reaches a customer.
    Operational safetyStale data stops conclusions and every human handoff arrives with context.
    Product valueVerified resolution improves without increasing repeat support or notification opt-outs.

    Berlin to Salzburg

    What the LLM does here

    The missed connection is already proven by a fixed calculation. The LLM handles the variable context around it.

    1Reads contextICE 1573, RJX 65, Munich transfer and traveller needs
    2Interprets optionsCompares journey fit, policy evidence, time, transfers and accessibility
    3Explains realityPresents viable choices in natural language without changing the booking
    FIXED RULE BEFORE LLM13:52 arrival − 13:18 departure = connection missed by 34 min
    OUTPUT CHECK AFTER LLMReject stale data, unsupported money claims and unusable alternatives
    Why a fixed rule is not enoughThe arithmetic proves the miss. It cannot interpret changing journey options, ticket scope, traveller constraints and the clearest way to explain those choices together.
